provenance.derivation: Composed in the manner of kasane no irome, for spring: 3 of our own published entries read as layers from the outermost inward — 春菜 haru-na (#BDD18E), then 深羊歯 fuka-shida (#4B6E43), then 枯枝 kare-eda (#65482E). NOT a historical combination: no layer is asserted to reproduce a documented Heian kasane, and no value was read from any kasane table. Chosen by hand, not generated. Adjacent layers are separated by ΔE00 33.3, 27.3 under @irodora/color-difference 0.1.0 — each above the ΔE00 5 at which the product calls two items the same (FR-44), because a layering whose edges cannot be told apart is not one. Weights fall inward (1, 0.8, 0.6, 0.5) because each inner layer shows less than the one over it.
provenance.editorialNotes: Early spring read from the outside in: the first greens (春菜) over a deeper fern (深羊歯), over the bare branch they grow from (枯枝). The pale layer is outermost because it is the season arriving; the brown is innermost because it is what the season is arriving over, showing only at the edge. The name is ours (芽吹, "Budding"), coined as a seasonal image the way the historical names are; it is not presented as a traditional kasane name.
